preconditions: Owned local Linux roots; real competing processes and explicit trusted ownership observations for uncertainty tests.
Explicit transaction-bound host authority; real stopped Linux processes and native root mutex for orphan recovery; independent normative byte oracle.
steps: Acquire shared native exclusion for writer/recovery kinds; recheck exact ownership and journal barriers before audited orphan removal.
Keep ordinary forced lock recovery blocked by a real crashed writer journal; use separately authorized transaction-bound takeover only for journal recovery and terminal cleanup.
Retain journals after ownership transfer alone and preserve foreign blockers across repeated real process stops.

oracle.requirement_contract: Ein Lock-Recovery-Befehl DARF NICHT ein vorhandenes Transaktionsjournal umgehen.
oracle.scope: Native lock and read-only observation libraries, journal-vetoed ordinary lock recovery and explicit transaction-bound audited recovery access. Ownership transfer alone does not remove any transaction or foreign blocker and cannot bypass an occupied native mutex. Full CLI/backend integration remains later work.

open_items: Complete native transaction/backend and CLI integrations in their later steps; validate the full runtime/target filesystem matrix in actual CI and target runs.
Native Linux local-filesystem scope is not a distributed/NFS lock or authenticated host identity.
